correctness.rationale: For every q>0 there are exactly three side and three vertex exterior chambers. The convex-hull visible-edge perimeter excess gives ellipse semiaxes (1+q/2,sqrt((1+q/2)^2-1)) and (2+q/2,sqrt((2+q/2)^2-1)). On the side extension the exact equation t+sqrt(t^2+2t+4)-2=q has a unique nonnegative solution t=q(q+4)/(2(q+3)), fixing every arc endpoint. The counterclockwise Green integrals I_f=a_f b_f(pi-2phi)+2h+th and I_v=2 a_v b_v psi-th sum with threefold symmetry to the boxed area. The q=0 limit and scaling were checked. The all-parameter proof is analytic; standard-library checker independently reconstructed convex hull perimeter and radially integrated area to agreement within 3e-6 at six q values.

value.rationale: A natural exact invariant of a foundational convex-geometric stochastic approximation construction is now determined for the equilateral triangle, the smallest noncentrally symmetric polygon. It is a complete finite-parameter area profile, not a fitted finite sample; six ellipse arc transitions and their Green integrals are explicit. The absence of a linear term and the exact q^{3/2} correction give a new sharp benchmark for small-parameter area excess in the polygonal Poisson-halfspace setting. No new general random expectation or arbitrary-polygon result is required for its motivated exact value.
